narrative.overview:
An art school graduate's digital atelier: deep-space dark backgrounds charged with electric blue and violet neon, surfaces that float rather than anchor, compositions that break the center axis on purpose. The layout is built on a two-column hero (lead + frosted status panel) and an asymmetric section grid with a sticky title column, never a centered top-to-bottom stack. This is work that makes a case through its own visual confidence.

The system rests on a single deep background layer (Ink Depth) with one luminous surface layer (Studio Dark), tied together by two neon accents: Electric Blue for interaction, Neon Orchid for gradients only. Ghost borders define edges without mass; glow is the only shadow.

It explicitly rejects: clean white Apple-style minimalism, flat SaaS enterprise layouts, warm cream tones, and academic resume formatting.
keyCharacteristics: Two-column hero: lead (name, intro, CTAs) + frosted status panel
Asymmetric section grid with a sticky left title column
Dual neon accents with strict roles: Electric Blue interaction, Neon Orchid gradients only
Glow is the only shadow; the hero name's resting glow is the single exception
Industrial-poster type: Archivo expanded headlines, Noto Sans SC body, JetBrains Mono labels
Glass reserved for two floating layers: nav bar and hero panel

rules.name: The No-Warm Rule
rules.body: No warm-tinted neutrals anywhere. Beige, sand, cream, parchment prohibited at any opacity. Every neutral stays cool-blue-shifted.

rules.name: The Two-Signal Rule
rules.body: Electric Blue is the primary interaction signal. Neon Orchid is structural, appearing only inside gradients alongside Electric Blue.

rules.name: The Expanded-Headline Rule
rules.body: All Latin display and headline type is pushed to font-stretch 125%. The width is the signature, not a decoration.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Earned Rule
rules.body: Monospace is reserved for genuinely technical content (skill names, labels, URLs, the developer tagline). Never for Chinese prose or as decorative texture.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Static section surfaces are flat at rest; depth comes from tone and border. Glow appears on interaction, with one exception.

rules.name: The Hero Glow Exception
rules.body: The hero name carries a resting neon glow as the page's single focal moment. It is the only static glow; every other glow must be earned by interaction.

rules.name: The Frosted Glass Exception
rules.body: backdrop-filter: blur is reserved for exactly two floating surfaces: the fixed nav bar and the hero status panel. All other surfaces stay solid.

dos: Do use Electric Blue for all links, hover states, and interactive signals.
Do use Ghost Borders (1px #ffffff10 to #ffffff14) as the default edge treatment.
Do activate neon on hover: border-color to Electric Blue + glow is the canonical signal.
Do treat motion as part of the visual language: entrance animations and hover transitions are expected.
Do use asymmetric composition deliberately: two-column hero, sticky title-column section grid.
Do reserve glass for the nav bar and hero panel; keep cards, tags, and contact blocks solid.
Do group skills by domain and give projects technical tags + an action link.
donts: Don't use warm beige, cream, sand, parchment, or ivory tones anywhere.
Don't design for white-background Apple-style minimalism.
Don't build a flat SaaS enterprise layout or a centered top-to-bottom stack.
Don't use academic or resume formatting.
Don't apply glassmorphism to static card or section surfaces (nav + hero panel only).
Don't use box-shadow as ambient decoration; glow is for interaction (hero name excepted).
Don't use Neon Orchid as a standalone flat accent color.
Don't use background-clip: text with gradient backgrounds for text coloring.
